## Sep 21 Results: The Numbers Don't Lie

Another day of profitable picks in the books. Our model went 2-1 on September 21st, posting a 66.7% win rate. When you're hitting above 65%, you're beating the market—that's just mathematical reality.

## Breaking Down the Data

Let's look at what the numbers tell us. The Tigers pick at 62% confidence was our strongest call of the day, and it delivered. The Giants squeaker at 50% was essentially a coin flip, but the model found the edge and we capitalized.

The Blue Jays miss at 51%? That's variance. When you're picking games at 51% probability, you expect to lose 49% of the time. That's literally within one standard deviation. No model goes perfect—we chase +EV over sample size.

## Sep 22 Preview: Tampa Bay Value Play

Tomorrow's slate brings us an interesting spot in the Bronx. The model has identified a 52% edge on the Tampa Bay Rays as road underdogs against the Yankees. Nick Martinez takes the ball for Tampa Bay against Carlos Rodón.

content.title: ⭐ Sep 22 Top Pick
content.value: Tampa Bay Rays @ New York Yankees

## The Martinez Factor

Nick Martinez has been quietly efficient this season. We're talking about a pitcher who limits hard contact and keeps his team in games. Against a Yankees lineup that's been feast-or-famine lately, that profile plays.

Rodón brings the strikeouts, but the consistency metrics show vulnerability. When you run the regression models and factor in recent form, park factors, and bullpen strength, that 52% number on Tampa Bay represents legitimate value.

Is 52% a massive edge? No. But in baseball, 52% sustained over volume is how you build bankroll. We're not looking for miracles—we're looking for math that works.

**The pick: Tampa Bay Rays at 52% confidence.**
